title: Credits Against Posted Employer Benefit Charging Charges
content:
A credit under Employer Benefit Charging reduces a charge already posted to an employer's position. The rules below govern every credit, whatever its reason.

## Credit rules

1. A credit always names the single posted charge it reduces, and never exceeds the remaining charge — the amount of that posted charge less every credit already booked against it.
2. A posted charge is credited back only once for each credit reason. Whether that charge already carries a credit for the same reason is judged from the Department's ledger record of credits naming that charge.
3. A cancelled payment credits the whole charge of that payment; a recovered overpayment credits the charges of the overpaid weeks in proportion to the principal recovered; an appeal decision relieving the employer credits as a relief does.
4. Credits appear on the next quarter's statement, or on the next reimbursement bill for a reimbursing employer.

The clause "A relief credits the whole remaining charge of every posting within the relief's scope" is **no longer in force** for the relief credit of a protest decision or of a determination on a separation response, each of which is now fixed on its own basis. A relief that an appeal decision grants still credits the whole remaining charge of every posting within the relief's scope, so an appeal decision relieving the employer credits that whole remaining charge.

## Credit reasons at a glance

| Credit reason | What is credited |
|---|---|
| Cancelled payment | The whole charge of that payment |
| Recovered overpayment | The charges of the overpaid weeks, in proportion to the principal recovered |
| Appeal reversal | As a relief credits: the whole remaining charge of every posting within the relief's scope |

## Hypothetical illustration of the cap and the once-per-reason rule

A posted charge of $200.00 already carries a recovered-overpayment credit of $50.00, so its remaining charge is $150.00.

- A further credit against that charge, for another reason, can be no more than $150.00.
- A second recovered-overpayment credit against that same charge is not posted, because the charge has already been credited once for that reason.

## Basis Q&A

*Where does a contributory employer see a credit?* On its next quarter's statement. A reimbursing employer sees it on its next reimbursement bill.
